NextItNet stacks causal dilated convolutions with residual connections, expanding history coverage without pooling ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). For stride-one convolutions, maximum receptive-field span is 1 + Σ(kℓ−1)dℓ along the longest path; exact reachable lags require tracing convolution taps and residual branches. Reachability does not imply equal influence: convolutional path multiplicity, learned weights and nonlinear gates shape the effective receptive field. General CNN research demonstrates this distinction; its Gaussian results should not be assumed to describe a particular causal NextItNet ([Luo et al.](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/file/c8067ad1937f728f51288b3eb986afaa-Paper.pdf)).

Suggested diagnostic controls, inferred from these architectural findings: preserve sequence length, left-padding, occupied positions and final nonpadding readout; replace or permute item identities in place rather than deleting and repacking histories. Compute lag-wise reachability and temporal path counts from the actual architecture, including skips and intermediate padding masks. Compare recent and distant perturbations within matched reachability/path-count strata where overlap exists; use unreachable positions as negative controls. If strata do not overlap, temporal preference and accessibility remain confounded. Measure trained sensitivity separately through embedding gradients and finite replacements.

Match corruption severity using equal numbers of changed positions, identical intervention types and replacement pools, and comparable embedding displacement and item frequency. Repeat across corruption doses and random draws, with identity/no-op controls; report paired score/rank changes alongside fixed-candidate validation HR@10. In-place shuffling preserves the selected item multiset and tests order sensitivity; replacement tests content sensitivity. These controls can reveal whether apparent recency dependence survives architectural and corruption matching, but do not by themselves establish a need for recency-based repair.
